# v0.9 — release preparation

Date: 2026-11-15. Status: source published; GitHub release validation pending.
Git tag convention: `v0.9`; FinOps Python package version: `0.9.0`.
This is a portfolio/lab release, not a production deployment certification.

## Publication update

The owner selected the public monorepo `workwithcrow12-art/cost-aware-gitops-platform`. Active workflows now live in `.github/workflows`, with component working directories and GitOps source paths adapted accordingly. Nested workflows are standalone examples and are not executed here.

Fresh local results: 42 FinOps tests, 1 mocked bootstrap test and 10 release/smoke fixture tests passed in WSL with isolated network/PID/mount namespaces, an empty allowlisted environment, read-only source/toolchain, UID/GID 65534 with no capabilities, 128 MiB writable scratch, 512 MiB address-space limit, 45 seconds CPU, 60 seconds wall-clock, 64 processes, 128 descriptors and 16 MiB maximum file size. The sandbox cleanup issue is resolved. The bootstrap test also passed after monorepo path migration.

The owner explicitly authorized ordinary GitHub-hosted release CI to download dependencies/toolchains/CVE databases and run tests/builds/scans. These CI runs are separate from the offline local audit harness. Required service, infrastructure, manifest and image checks must pass before tagging `v0.9`. Tag publication verifies a successful validation run for the current main SHA, then scans/publishes images and creates the GitHub release. AWS provisioning is excluded.

The initial source push is for CI validation, not a claim of release readiness. The earlier preparation record below is retained as history; the single-repository decision supersedes its five-remote instructions.

## Changes

- Payment service no longer writes the full charge request, including card number and CVV, to INFO logs. The storefront remains a mock payment application. If real card data was previously entered, existing logs require separate access/retention review; this patch does not remove historical logs.
- Frontend session/currency cookies use the application base path, including logout deletion. Product deep links can retain the same cart session. Platform and deployment metadata are published safely for concurrent requests.
- Both Go money packages return zero for a zero multiplier and reject invalid fractional values in sign predicates. Checkout currency conversion now keeps request cancellation.
- FinOps rejects nonfinite OpenCost/CUR amounts and malformed OpenCost allocation containers before producing a report. Negative credits and zero remain valid.
- FinOps release images must pass a HIGH/CRITICAL Trivy vulnerability scan before push. The optional GitOps reporter now references `v0.9`; enable it only after that image is published.
- Added regression test sources for these changes. Their execution remains pending.

Browser cookies created by the old deep-link behavior may need clearing after upgrade. The optional shopping assistant is not deployed by the base manifests; its HTTP response-body cleanup remains outside these fixes and must be addressed before enabling that feature.

## Evidence and limits

This was a focused source review, not the full security-audit workflow. No claim is made that all vulnerabilities were found or that dependencies are free of current CVEs. Inspected Terraform/GitOps boundaries did not yield a confirmed exploitable defect in this pass; deployment settings remain unverified.

Static checks in this session: 14 FinOps Python files parsed with `ast.parse`, package TOML parsed with version `0.9.0`, payment JavaScript syntax checked with `node --check`, and tracked worktree diffs checked for whitespace errors. These checks do not execute the new regression tests.

The requested security-audit skill requires OS-enforced network isolation, an allowlisted empty environment, read-only source/toolchain, scratch-only writes and explicit resource limits for target execution. Those controls were not available here: Docker was not found and WSL inventory returned access denied. No project tests, builds, dependency installation, cloud probes or notifications were executed. A passing historical test record is not evidence for these changes.

## Required before publishing v0.9

1. Validate in a disposable isolated environment with preloaded toolchains/dependencies, no network or credentials and the skill's resource/filesystem limits. Run FinOps lint and its full unittest suite; payment `npm test`; frontend and checkout `go test -race ./...`; and the remaining existing service suites. Format/check Go sources using the pinned toolchain.
2. Run the existing infrastructure mock validations, manifest rendering and Kyverno gates. Separately run trusted image builds/scans in the release infrastructure and retain their results. Resolve any HIGH/CRITICAL image findings; do not bypass the new gate.
3. Configure the five independent Git repositories (`platform-infra`, `gitops-config`, `boutique-app`, `finops-toolkit`, `.github`) with the intended owner/remotes. At review time each had no commits and no origin configured, with substantial pre-existing staged/untracked work. Review the complete initial contents before committing. The outer workspace is not a release repository.
4. Configure branch protections, required checks, CODEOWNERS/reviewers and GitHub environments/OIDC/secrets as documented. Replace example organization URLs where needed. Publish initial branches and require fresh CI success before creating release tags.
5. Create `v0.9` on the verified commits and record each repository SHA in the release. Publish the FinOps image successfully before enabling its reporter. Build/promote the patched Boutique images: the GitOps base still uses upstream digest-pinned images, so editing source alone does not deploy these fixes.
6. For an actual cluster deployment, perform the documented bootstrap, secret provisioning, checkout smoke and canary/rollback exercise. Verify external notifications, private-cluster access, persistence and recovery separately.

No commits, tags, remote pushes, GitHub releases or cloud deployments were created by this review.
